findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed two sanitizer buckets at the bar measure 0ppm quaternary ammonia with a test strip. The PIC repeated the test with her own strip, also measuring 0ppm. The PIC informed bar staff and the buckets were replaced. Ensure sanitizer concentration is monitored with test strips and the buckets are replaced frequently to prevent improper sanitizing of food contact surfaces.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment:
Observed the following food items out of the appropriate temperature range:
1. Garlic cream sauce - sauté hot cooler
2. Chicken breast - sauté hot cooler - 45F, probe
3. Piccata sauce - sauté sauce cooler
4. Jambalaya - sauté sauce cooler - 48F, probe
5. Cut tomatoes - sauté sauce cooler
6. Sliced cheese - sauté sauce cooler
7 Whipped cream - dessert cooler

The inspector was present directly after lunch rush, so the coolers were open for an extended time during service. The coolers were closed and left to cool during the rest of the inspection. The inspector returned at the end of the inspection (roughly 1 hour later) and the dessert cooler was able to reach proper cold holding temperatures. The sauté hot cooler, however, failed to cool within the timeframe. 

CORRECTED - The PIC was informed, and all time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods within the cooler were discarded. The staff plan to cease use of the cooler until it can be repaired or replaced.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment:
Observed that the temperatures from multiple coolers on the cook-line were too high. Since they were in the middle of their lunch rush, we waited approximately 30 minutes after advising cook staff to keep covers closed on coolers to re-probe food. Some food items chilled to an appropriate temperature in that time. The food items that were still too hot are listed below : 
1. Dairy-based sauces (53F) - Broiler prep cooler top
2. Mayo (52F) - Broiler prep cooler top
3. Cut tomatoes (49F) - Broiler prep cooler top
4. Cut lettuce (50F) - Broiler prep cooler top
5. Bleu cheese (50F) - Broiler prep cooler top
6. Whipped cream (54F) - Dessert prep cooler
7. Chicken (50F) - Dessert prep cooler

All food items listed above were voluntarily discarded by the PIC. The broiler prep cooler was directly across from multiple operating broilers, and the area was very hot. Advised PIC to swap from temperature control to time as a control for time/temperature control (TCS) foods in that cooler. Cook staff already have an effective time keeping system in place for time as a control monitoring/labeling. Items in dessert cooler were advised to be placed in another cooler that holds temp more effectively, as those two food items are the only TCS foods stored there. The bottom of both coolers were well cooled (~35F), so advised cook staff to keep covers on cooler tops closed as frequently as possible to retain refrigeration. Inspector will perform a spot-check on 2/26/25 to ensure time as a control is being implemented correctly and remaining TCS foods in coolers are being maintained at the appropriate temperatures (less than 41F).
